issue.title: fix(hy): publish the native store write lock during writes
issue.body:
## Problem

`native_store_read_slot()` refuses reads while `native_store_write_lock()` is held, but no writer ever acquired that lock. The bridge serialized its own writes with `_write_lock` and never exposed them to the read slot, so the "no native read during a write" guard was dead code.

## Fix

Hold `native_store_write_lock` around `ingest`, `ingest_extracted`, `update` and `delete`. Add a regression that starts a bridge update and asserts the read slot reports not-admitted until it finishes.

## Verification

- `bash memhub/scripts/run-tests-isolated.sh core tests/test_native_store_write_lock.py` → 1 passed

comment.body:
Maintainer decision: we will **not** merge this.

Activating `native_store_write_lock` during writes would enforce a “no native read while writing” guard that we do not want for MemHub’s default path. HY memory work is dominated by network I/O (embed/LLM); real store touch time is short, and concurrent read+write is expected. This lock was mainly a Chroma/GIL fail-fast; for our stack it is unnecessary friction.

Follow-up: open a PR that **removes** `native_store_read_slot` / `native_store_write_lock` entirely (instead of wiring the write side). Please close this once that lands, or we can close it as superseded.

issue.title: fix(freshness): accept segment support refs in the freshness proof
issue.body:
## Problem

Long Evidence records are split into segments, and their support refs carry `segment_index` / `segment_start` / `segment_end` / `segment_hash` — all part of `TaskEvidenceRef` in `memory_tasks.py`.

The freshness validator hard-coded only the four base keys. One such proof raised `memory_freshness_invalid_reference`, the UDF error surfaced as `sqlite3.OperationalError`, and `/api/v1/memory-library` returned 503 for the whole page. This is the root cause reported in #74 item 1.

## Fix

Derive the allowed key set from `TaskEvidenceRef` itself, so a future optional field cannot silently make every proof invalid. Add a regression with a valid segment ref.

## Verification

- `bash memhub/scripts/run-tests-isolated.sh core tests/test_memory_evidence_freshness.py` → 28 passed

Refs #74

comment.body: 跟进：拆除新鲜度读路径的 PR 已开 → 见同仓库 `chore/retire-memory-freshness`（retire memory evidence freshness）。本 PR（#86）仍建议关闭、不要合并。

issue.title: [Bug] Codex import: >2 GiB session file reported as unsupported_schema, Codex stores 0 records
issue.body:
**TL;DR（中文）**：Codex 会话目录里有一个超过 2 GiB 的 rollout 文件。发现阶段对它抛出 `FILE_TOO_LARGE`，但 `discovery_failure_code()` 把它映射成 `unsupported_schema`，所以界面和 CLI 显示的是"格式不支持"，而不是"文件过大"。导入开始约 50 分钟后，Codex 仍然是 0 条入库，而 Claude Code / Hermes / OpenCode 在同一时间段内都正常导入。

---

# Codex import: a >2 GiB session file is reported as `unsupported_schema`, and Codex stores 0 records

## Environment

- MemHub app 1.0.4, Runtime 1.0.4 (build 13, darwin-arm64), macOS arm64
- Codex CLI 0.160.0
- `~/.codex/sessions`: 148 rollout `.jsonl` files, 7.3 GB in total. Median file is about 3 MB, 5 files are over 256 MB, and **1 file is 3,221,520,570 bytes (over 2 GiB)**. It is a single long-running session.
- Sources were authorized from the desktop onboarding ("import history") for Claude Code, Codex, Hermes and OpenCode at the same time.

## What happens

1. Every Codex live-sync run ends with exactly one `import.parse.issue_summary` event (`reason: unsupported_schema`, `count: 1`). It scans 147 targets, stores 0 records, and live sync switches to `degraded` (`live_sync_import_errors`). This happened 25 times in about 50 minutes, about 50 s per run.
2. The Codex `history` job stays `pending` (`discovered: 6`, `errors: 6`, `stored: 0`), and no `import.*` log events reference its job id.
3. In the same window, Claude Code, Hermes and OpenCode imported thousands of records without errors.

## Why the label is `unsupported_schema`

- `imports/access.py`: discovery raises `SourceAccessErrorCode.FILE_TOO_LARGE` when `st_size > max_file_bytes`, where `DEFAULT_MAX_SOURCE_FILE_BYTES = 2 GiB`.
- `imports/sources/common.py`: `discovery_failure_code()` returns `BUDGET_EXCEEDED` for budget errors and **`UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA` for everything else**, including `FILE_TOO_LARGE`. `_scan_failure_code()` maps the open path the same way. `ScanIssueCode.FILE_TOO_LARGE` exists but is not used on these paths.
- The only file over 2 GiB in the directory lines up with the single error in every sync run.

The reader already handles large files: the comment in `common.py` explains that large Codex files are read in bounded slices, because skipping them dropped 85% of the history bytes. The 2 GiB access gate still rejects the file before the reader gets a chance.

## Expected

- A file over the access limit is reported as `file_too_large`, not `unsupported_schema`, so users can see what to do.
- One oversized file does not block or degrade the rest of the Codex source. Ideally files over 2 GiB are read in bounded slices like the other large files.
- If the pending `history` job is waiting on something else, please make that visible. We could not tell from the CLI or the logs why it never started.

I can provide more diagnostics if needed (job rows, `import_issues`, `logs export`).

issue.title: fix(web): accept user-selected sources after a committed upload
issue.body:
## Summary

`HistoryImport.reviewSource()` refreshed the source list after a file was committed and then accepted only `default` and `environment_override`:

```ts
!["default", "environment_override"].includes(source.candidate_kind)
```

A directory the person picked through the directory picker is `user_selected` (the contract's third value, also emitted by the Core). The same build therefore offered that directory during import and rejected it immediately after saving the file, with `source_identity_unavailable`. The committed upload stayed on disk while the review step could never complete.

This replaces the hand-written pair with a set covering every value `SourceResponse["candidate_kind"]` can hold, and adds a regression that uploads, commits, reviews a `user_selected` source, grants consent, and connects it.

## Scope

This is the source path. The shipped 1.0.4 bundle has a similar stale check elsewhere (issue #74 item 2); this PR does not rebuild the bundle, but it stops the checked-in web source from rejecting the same value.

## Verification

The new test fails on `main` (the review step shows `source_identity_unavailable` and no consent checkbox appears) and passes with the change:

```bash
cd memhub/apps/web && pnpm vitest run src/HistoryImport.test.tsx
# 49 passed
```

`pnpm --filter @one-memory/web typecheck` and `biome check` on both files pass.

Refs #74.

comment.body: 关闭：历史内部路径，App 无入口，不支持用户自定义上传。

感谢提交。

issue.title: fix(freshness): accept segment support refs in the freshness proof
issue.body:
## Problem

Long Evidence records are split into segments, and their support refs carry `segment_index` / `segment_start` / `segment_end` / `segment_hash` — all part of `TaskEvidenceRef` in `memory_tasks.py`.

The freshness validator hard-coded only the four base keys. One such proof raised `memory_freshness_invalid_reference`, the UDF error surfaced as `sqlite3.OperationalError`, and `/api/v1/memory-library` returned 503 for the whole page. This is the root cause reported in #74 item 1.

## Fix

Derive the allowed key set from `TaskEvidenceRef` itself, so a future optional field cannot silently make every proof invalid. Add a regression with a valid segment ref.

## Verification

- `bash memhub/scripts/run-tests-isolated.sh core tests/test_memory_evidence_freshness.py` → 28 passed

Refs #74

comment.body:
感谢提交。

我们重新评估了这条路径：**记忆新鲜度（evidence freshness proof）整体属于过度设计**——业务层用 proof / support_refs / 分段字段在读路径上逐条回查 evidence 是否被改，成本和复杂度高，收益却只是「证据改过就藏掉这条 memory」。业务层再为 HY 窗口做 segment，还把 OpenAI 形 messages 切段塞进 SDK，和 SDK 自身阶段处理叠床架屋，#86 这类「允许 segment_* key」只会继续加固这套设计。

**结论：不合并本 PR。我们计划删除新鲜度校验这一设计**（读路径不再做 `is_memory_evidence_current` / proof 核对），而不是继续修 segment 兼容。后续会另开拆除工作；本 PR 可关闭或保持 open 作对照，请不要再往 freshness 上叠字段兼容。
